semantic_checks.finding: The selected coefficient obtains H from the actual selected complete-active-face construction. Its proved supporting indices show j,l,index(i) are H-active, and R.active={j,l} gives a genuine ridge/face incidence. The source then instantiates the proved canonical coefficient adapter; H incidence and common mass are not supplied as target identities.

A strict ridge witness and original actual facet geometry derive native pair nonparallelity. The named ridge angle is proved equal to raw arccos(dot uj ul) using the two distinct original facet indices and the actual complete active pair. No new angle or multiplicity constant is introduced.

The selected-face Green formula starts from the genuine P.native_Green identity, replaces the actual leading term with the independently proved q2 canonical ridge leading, and replaces each boundary coefficient by its complete-H canonical coefficient. Signed support distance and the minus boundary sign are preserved termwise.

The selected complete face is built from a real original-polyhedron point with j,l,index(i) active and all other selected residual facets strict. Positive proportionality of any additional active retained residual is derived from exact equivalent presentations and their actual normal cones. Consequently the complete active normal space has rank 3, even with arbitrarily many active original facet labels.

Distinct selected tangent facets map injectively to complete actual faces: if two faces agreed, the second selected index would be active at the first selected point, contradicting its strictness there. This is not injection of arbitrary original facet labels or an assumption of simple vertices.

Every actual codimension-three face incident to the pair contains an active original index outside the pair by its normal rank. Its double residual is nonzero, from original actual-facet affine inconsistency and its true supporting level. If all selected constraints were strict at that point, the active proper retained normal would be an outward normal in the zero cone of an interior selected stratum, a contradiction. Thus some selected facet is active.

The supporting-index uniqueness argument identifies the selected complete closed face with any incident H containing its selected index. It uses the spanning three original supporting levels and the injective correspondence between complete active sets and their nonempty exact-stratum closed faces. The finite selectedFaceAtPair map is therefore genuinely bijective, and its Equiv.sum_comp identity counts each incident H once.

Actual.native_Green_actualFaces uses that actual finite equivalence to replace the selected sum by the sum over the subtype of all H containing j and l. No abstract equinumerosity, ordered triple multiplicity or assumed surface sum is used.

For the complementary H subtype, the failure of j-and-l membership implies R.active is not contained in H.active. The explicitly defined nonincident actual conormal is zero, so the complete signed coefficient is zero. Fintype.sum_subtype_add_sum_subtype then extends the incident sum to the sum over every actual codimension-three face without extra terms.

The final public theorem has only original unit normals, an original strict interior, original irredundancy witnesses, distinct pair indices and an actual codimension-two face with complete active set {j,l}. A genuine strict ridge witness follows from the actual face representative, and the exact selected tangent presentation is constructed internally. No presentation, generic regularity, Fatou sequence or Green identity is an input.

The four exported types and their actual 480-node dependency graph introduce no threshold-AE Green, threshold-AE pair regularity, old all-threshold Fatou continuation or old final ridge-estimate supplier. Pointwise fixed-threshold geometric and analytic identities are the proof route.

The resulting statement is the per-actual-ridge version of the printed edge Green formula, with one named actual ridge leading term and the canonical signed sum over every H. The global half-ordered-pair to actual-ridge sum and final spherical estimate remain separate assembly steps; this bounded review does not silently certify those additional steps.
